# Field

The wrapper that turns any control into a labelled form field. Field generates the id, htmlFor and aria-describedby wiring for you and cascades error and disabled state to the control inside.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputField placeholder="you@example.com" type="email" />
  </InputRoot>
  <FieldHint>We'll only use it for account notifications.</FieldHint>
</Field>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add field
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/field/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

Drop a control between `FieldLabel` and `FieldHint`. You never touch `id`, `htmlFor`, or `aria-describedby` - `Field` generates them with `useId` and hands them to the control through context. Clicking the label focuses the control, and screen readers announce the hint.

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { Field, FieldLabel, FieldHint } from "@/components/ui/field"
import { InputRoot, InputField } from "@/components/ui/input"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
      <InputRoot>
        <InputField type="email" />
      </InputRoot>
      <FieldHint>We'll only use it for account notifications.</FieldHint>
    </Field>
  )
}
```

## Required & error

Set `required` to append a destructive asterisk to the label. Set `hasError` on the `Field` - it cascades to the control’s border, sets `aria-invalid`, and turns the hint into the destructive error message. You set it in one place, not on every part.

```tsx
<Field required>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputField defaultValue="wrong@" type="email" />
  </InputRoot>
</Field>

<Field hasError required>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputField defaultValue="wrong@" type="email" />
  </InputRoot>
  <FieldHint>Enter a valid email address.</FieldHint>
</Field>
```

## Validation

Put the constraint on the control: `required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`, `minLength`. Inside a `Form`, a failed submit shows the message in the field, focuses the first invalid control and shakes it. No browser bubble. `FieldError` with `match` gives each failure its own copy, and takes the hint's place while it shows.

```tsx
<Form onFormSubmit={save}>
  <Field>
    <FieldLabel required>Email</FieldLabel>
    <InputRoot>
      <InputField name="email" type="email" required />
    </InputRoot>
    <FieldHint>We send the receipt here.</FieldHint>
    <FieldError match="valueMissing">Enter your email.</FieldError>
    <FieldError match="typeMismatch">That email is missing an @ or a domain.</FieldError>
  </Field>

  <Field>
    <FieldLabel required>Postcode</FieldLabel>
    <InputRoot>
      <InputField name="postcode" required pattern="[0-9]{5}" />
    </InputRoot>
    <FieldError match="valueMissing">Enter a postcode.</FieldError>
    <FieldError match="patternMismatch">Use five digits.</FieldError>
  </Field>

  <FormActions>
    <Button type="submit">Continue</Button>
  </FormActions>
</Form>
```

Skip `FieldError` and the field shows the browser's own message. Leave out `match` and one `FieldError` shows whatever failed.

## Custom validation

`validate` runs once the native constraints pass. It gets the value and every value in the form, and returns a message, a list of them, or `null`.

```tsx
<Field
  validate={(value) => {
    const errors = []
    if (value.length < 8) errors.push("Use at least 8 characters.")
    if (!/[0-9]/.test(value)) errors.push("Add a number.")
    return errors
  }}
>
  <FieldLabel required>Password</FieldLabel>
  <InputRoot><InputField name="password" type="password" /></InputRoot>
  <FieldHint>8 characters and a number.</FieldHint>
</Field>

<Field validate={(value, values) => (value === values.password ? null : "The passwords don't match.")}>
  <FieldLabel required>Confirm password</FieldLabel>
  <InputRoot><InputField name="confirm" type="password" /></InputRoot>
</Field>
```

## Async validation

Return a promise to check against your API. Pair it with `validationDebounceTime` so a request waits for a pause in typing. A stale answer never overwrites a newer one, and a submit waits for pending checks. `data-validating` is on the Field while one runs.

```tsx
<Form validationMode="onChange" validationDebounceTime={300} onFormSubmit={claim}>
  <Field validate={checkUsername} className="group/field">
    <FieldLabel required>Username</FieldLabel>
    <InputRoot>
      <InputField name="username" />
      <InputSuffix className="hidden group-data-validating/field:flex">
        <Spinner aria-hidden />
      </InputSuffix>
    </InputRoot>
    <FieldHint>Checked as you type.</FieldHint>
  </Field>
</Form>

async function checkUsername(value) {
  const res = await fetch("/api/username?q=" + encodeURIComponent(value))
  const { taken } = await res.json()
  return taken ? "That username is taken." : null
}
```

## Field states

The Field root carries its state as data attributes, so you can style anything inside it: `data-invalid`, `data-valid`, `data-touched`, `data-dirty`, `data-filled`, `data-focused` and `data-validating`.

```tsx
<Field className="group/field">
  <FieldLabel className="group-data-focused/field:text-foreground">Email</FieldLabel>
  …
</Field>
```

## Any control

`Field` is control-agnostic. Because Input, Select, and PasswordInput all forward native props, the same wrapper labels any of them - the wiring lands on the right element automatically.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Country</FieldLabel>
  <Select>
    <SelectTrigger>
      <SelectValue placeholder="Select a country" />
    </SelectTrigger>
    <SelectContent>
      <SelectItem value="es">Spain</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="fr">France</SelectItem>
      <SelectItem value="de">Germany</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
</Field>

<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Password</FieldLabel>
  <PasswordInput placeholder="Create a password" />
  <FieldHint>At least 8 characters.</FieldHint>
</Field>
```

## Two fields per row

`FieldRow` places sibling fields side by side and stacks them on narrow viewports - the answer to *Name · Surname* pairs. It is pure layout, so it composes with any number of fields.

```tsx
<FieldRow>
  <Field>
    <FieldLabel>First name</FieldLabel>
    <InputRoot><InputField placeholder="Ada" /></InputRoot>
  </Field>
  <Field>
    <FieldLabel>Last name</FieldLabel>
    <InputRoot><InputField placeholder="Lovelace" /></InputRoot>
  </Field>
</FieldRow>
```

## A whole form

Wrap the fields in a [`Form`](https://www.koalaui.com/docs/components/form.md), which owns the gap so no form has to invent its own, reach for `FieldRow` where two values belong together, and let each `Field` own its own wiring. This is a full registration form, name pair, email, country, and a password pair, with nothing wired by hand.

```tsx
<Form>
  <FieldRow>
    <Field required>
      <FieldLabel>First name</FieldLabel>
      <InputRoot><InputField placeholder="Ada" /></InputRoot>
    </Field>
    <Field required>
      <FieldLabel>Last name</FieldLabel>
      <InputRoot><InputField placeholder="Lovelace" /></InputRoot>
    </Field>
  </FieldRow>

  <Field required>
    <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
    <InputRoot><InputField placeholder="ada@example.com" type="email" /></InputRoot>
    <FieldHint>We'll send a confirmation link here.</FieldHint>
  </Field>

  <Field required>
    <FieldLabel>Country</FieldLabel>
    <Select>
      <SelectTrigger>
        <SelectValue placeholder="Select a country" />
      </SelectTrigger>
      <SelectContent>
        <SelectItem value="es">Spain</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="fr">France</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="de">Germany</SelectItem>
        <SelectItem value="uk">United Kingdom</SelectItem>
      </SelectContent>
    </Select>
  </Field>

  <FieldRow>
    <Field required>
      <FieldLabel>Password</FieldLabel>
      <PasswordInput placeholder="Create a password" />
    </Field>
    <Field required>
      <FieldLabel>Confirm password</FieldLabel>
      <PasswordInput placeholder="Repeat it" />
    </Field>
  </FieldRow>

  <FormActions align="stack" className="mt-1">
    <Button type="submit">Create account</Button>
  </FormActions>
</Form>
```

## In a Dialog

`Field` composes straight into a Dialog. The wiring flows through Radix's Portal because React context follows the component tree, not the DOM - so `htmlFor`, `aria-describedby`, and the `hasError` cascade all still work. The modal's own name comes from `DialogTitle` / `DialogDescription` (Radix), independent of the per-field labels. Try submitting with an invalid email to see the error cascade.

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger asChild>
    <Button>Create account</Button>
  </DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent size="md">
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Create your account</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>It takes less than a minute.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>

    <FormSection>
      <FieldRow>
        <Field required>
          <FieldLabel>First name</FieldLabel>
          <InputRoot><InputField placeholder="Ada" /></InputRoot>
        </Field>
        <Field required>
          <FieldLabel>Last name</FieldLabel>
          <InputRoot><InputField placeholder="Lovelace" /></InputRoot>
        </Field>
      </FieldRow>

      <Field required hasError={!!emailError}>
        <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
        <InputRoot><InputField type="email" value={email} onChange={…} /></InputRoot>
        <FieldHint>{emailError ?? "We'll send a confirmation link here."}</FieldHint>
      </Field>

      <Field required>
        <FieldLabel>Country</FieldLabel>
        <Select>
          <SelectTrigger><SelectValue placeholder="Select a country" /></SelectTrigger>
          <SelectContent>{/* …items */}</SelectContent>
        </Select>
      </Field>

      <Field required>
        <FieldLabel>Password</FieldLabel>
        <PasswordInput placeholder="Create a password" />
        <FieldHint>At least 8 characters.</FieldHint>
      </Field>
    </FormSection>

    <DialogFooter>
      <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
      <Button>Create account</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` on the `Field` dims the label and disables the control inside.

```tsx
<Field disabled>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <InputRoot>
    <InputField placeholder="you@example.com" />
  </InputRoot>
</Field>
```

## Field vs FieldGroup

A Field wraps *one* control, because a `label` needs exactly one control to point at. When several controls answer a single question, a radio set or a cluster of checkboxes, there is nothing for the label to name, so the right wrapper is [`FieldGroup`](https://www.koalaui.com/docs/components/form.md): a real `fieldset` with a real `legend`. It ships alongside Field and takes the same `hasError`, `disabled`, and `required` props, and the same `FieldHint` describes the whole group.

```tsx
// One control: a Field.
<Field required>
  <FieldLabel>Email</FieldLabel>
  <InputRoot><InputField type="email" /></InputRoot>
</Field>

// Several controls, one question: a FieldGroup.
<FieldGroup required>
  <FieldGroupLabel>Email preferences</FieldGroupLabel>
  <RadioGroup>…</RadioGroup>
  <FieldHint>Pick at least one.</FieldHint>
</FieldGroup>
```

## API reference

### Field

One labelled control. Renders a `div` and forwards its props. Generates the ids, wires `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, and validates the control inside.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hasError | boolean | - | Forces the error state and wins over anything computed. Leave it unset to let native constraints, `validate` and server `errors` decide. |
| required | boolean | false | Appends a destructive asterisk to the label. Put `required` on the control too for the check itself. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Dims the label, disables the control and skips validation. |
| name | string | - | The key for this field's value and server errors. Defaults to the control's `name`. |
| validate | (value: unknown, formValues: FormValues) => string \| string[] \| null \| Promise<…> | - | Runs after native constraints pass. Return a message, several, or `null` when valid. |
| validationMode | "onSubmit" \| "onBlur" \| "onChange" | - | Overrides the Form's mode for this field. |
| validationDebounceTime | number | - | Overrides the Form's debounce for this field, in ms. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-invalid | Present while the field is invalid. `data-error` mirrors it. |
| data-valid | Present once the field has been validated and passed. |
| data-validating | Present while an async `validate` is pending. |
| data-touched | Present once focus has left the field. |
| data-dirty | Present when the value differs from the initial one. |
| data-filled | Present when the control has a value. |
| data-focused | Present while focus is inside the field. |
| data-disabled | Present when the field is disabled. |

### FieldLabel

The shared `Label`, wired to the field's control through `htmlFor`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| required | boolean | - | Appends the asterisk. Inherited from the Field. |
| disabled | boolean | - | Dims the label. Inherited from the Field. |

### FieldHint

The shared `Hint`: helper text that describes the control. An error takes its place while it shows.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hasError | boolean | - | Switches to the destructive tone. Inherited from the Field. |

### FieldError

The error message. Without one, the Field renders its own. Describes the control through `aria-describedby` while it shows.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| match | "valueMissing" \| "typeMismatch" \| "patternMismatch" \| "tooShort" \| "tooLong" \| "rangeUnderflow" \| "rangeOverflow" \| "stepMismatch" \| "badInput" \| "customError" \| boolean | - | Show only for one validity state. `customError` covers `validate` and server errors. `true` always shows. |
| children | ReactNode | - | Your copy. Without it, the field's own message (the browser's, your validator's or the server's). |

### FieldGroup

Several controls answering one question: a real `fieldset`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hasError | boolean | false | Destructive tone on the hint, `aria-invalid` on the fieldset. |
| disabled | boolean | false | Natively disables every control inside. |
| required | boolean | false | Appends the asterisk to the legend. |

### FieldGroupLabel

The group's `legend`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| required | boolean | - | Appends the asterisk. Inherited from the group. |

### FieldRow

Sibling fields on one line, stacked below `sm`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| columns | 2 \| 3 | 2 | Columns from `sm` up. |

## FAQ

### What wiring does Field actually generate for me?

Field calls useId to mint stable ids and hands them through context to its parts: FieldLabel gets the matching htmlFor, the control gets the id, and FieldHint gets pointed at by aria-describedby. You never set id, htmlFor, or aria-describedby yourself.

### How does a control opt into the Field context?

Controls read the Field context to receive their id, aria, and error or disabled state, which is why Input, Select, and PasswordInput just work inside a Field. Field never inspects child types across the server to client boundary, so any control that consumes the context picks up the wiring automatically.

### Does Field validate on its own?

Yes. It checks the native constraints on its control (required, type, pattern, minLength and the rest), then your validate function. Inside a Form, the Form decides when that runs and blocks a submit that fails. Outside one, a plain form's own validation still shows the message in the field.

### Do hasError and FieldHint still work?

Yes. An explicit hasError wins over anything the field computed, and the FieldHint turns destructive as before. Setting hasError also tells the field you own the message, so it does not render one of its own.

### Where do I set the error state, on the Field or on each part?

Set `hasError` once on the Field. It cascades to the control's border, sets aria-invalid on the control, and turns the FieldHint into a destructive error message, so you never repeat the flag on every part.

### What do the required and disabled props do?

`required` appends a destructive asterisk to the FieldLabel. `disabled` dims the label and disables the control inside, again set in one place on the Field rather than on each part.

### Why is aria-describedby only present when there is a hint?

FieldHint registers itself on mount, so Field only advertises aria-describedby when a hint is actually rendered and never points the control at a missing node. Because it registers on mount rather than by inspecting child types, SSR and the first client render agree and there is no hydration mismatch.

### Does Field still wire correctly inside a Dialog or other portal?

Yes. React context follows the component tree, not the DOM, so htmlFor, aria-describedby, and the hasError cascade all keep working through Radix's Portal. The dialog's own accessible name comes from DialogTitle and DialogDescription, independent of the per-field labels.

### How do I place two fields side by side?

Wrap sibling Fields in FieldRow. It is pure layout with no context, laying fields out in a grid that stacks to one column on narrow viewports, so it composes with any number of fields. Pass columns={3} for a three-up row; the default is 2.

### Can I put a RadioGroup or a checkbox cluster in a Field?

Use FieldGroup instead. A Field wraps one control because a label needs exactly one control to point at, while several controls answering a single question need a fieldset and legend, which is what FieldGroup renders. A single checkbox, like 'I agree to the terms', is still one control, so that one is a Field.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add field` writes `components/ui/field/`. Import from `@/components/ui/field`:

- Components and helpers: `Field`, `FieldError`, `FieldLabel`, `FieldHint`, `FieldGroup`, `FieldGroupLabel`, `FieldRow`, `fieldVariants`, `fieldGroupVariants`
- Types: `FieldProps`, `FieldErrorProps`, `FieldValidity`, `FieldValidityKey`, `FieldLabelProps`, `FieldHintProps`, `FieldGroupProps`, `FieldGroupLabelProps`, `FieldRowProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `label`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `field-context`, `field-group-context`, `form-context`, `motion`, `tv`
